Occupational asthma and work-related asthma are indeed different manifestations of the same disease, with occupational asthma being more related to exposure to specific allergens at work. Explanation: Occupational asthma is a type of work-related asthma that arises from an individual's exposure to specific allergens in their work environment. It's not the same as non-occupational or idiopathic (spontaneous) asthma, which has no known trigger. The given statement correctly identifies occupational asthma as a distinct condition within the broader category of work-related asthma.

Spirometry before and after bronchodilator use should be routinely performed to assess bronchial obstruction, confirming whether the child has asthma or another condition causing airflow limitation. 3. Allergy evaluation with total IgE measurement, immediate-reading skin tests, or serum specific IgE can help determine if one or more allergens are involved in the pathophysiology of asthma by identifying potential allergens that trigger or exacerbate symptoms. 4.
